# [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas

## Summary

Implement #58240. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` currently keeps an independent CPU prefix cache
in each DP replica. When a request is routed to another local replica, that replica recomputes
a prefix even though a completed CPU copy is available. This change adds an opt-in
`cpu_offload_shared=true` mode that lets local DP replicas reuse completed CPU prefixes.

This builds on [#37160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37160), which
introduced `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` and its private per-replica CPU cache.
This PR extends that connector with opt-in cross-DP publication and lookup; it
does not change the native offloader's per-replica semantics.

## Configuration

Add `cpu_offload_shared`, a JSON boolean in `kv_connector_extra_config`,
defaulting to `false`. Set it to `true` to share completed CPU prefixes with
compatible DP replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group.
Leaving it unset retains the existing private CPU pools.

The CPU capacity remains a per-worker budget: `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank`
reserves each worker's write partition. Corresponding local DP peers can read
published entries from one another's partitions, while writes remain owned by
the worker that allocates the slot. For example, two local DP peers configured
with 8 GiB each expose a 16 GiB node-local region for published slots and
metadata; this is shared visibility, not a dynamically rebalanced write pool.

Pass the following to `--kv-transfer-config`:

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "cpu_offload_shared": true,
    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
    "lazy_offload": false
  }
}
```

Shared mode requires the CPU backend, eager offloading (`lazy_offload=false`),
prefix caching, compatible model/KV layouts and reproducible prefix hashes.
It supports fixed MoE DP groups and TP, with `PP=DCP=PCP=1` and no LoRA or
elastic EP. Each TP coordinate shares its own KV shard with corresponding
local DP peers. Cross-node transfer requires a network-capable connector or tier.

## Implementation

Use the existing `SharedOffloadRegion` type, as established for native
`CPUOffloadingSpec` storage by
[#50094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50094), and the DMA/`BlockPool`
interfaces for storage and transfers; the cross-DP publication index, locking
and reader reference semantics are new code in this PR. Each writer owns a
fixed partition, and the shared pool does not dynamically move free write slots
between workers. Lookup and pinning use `flock` on the metadata region's descriptor;
prefixes are published after all worker stores complete, and reader references
prevent slot reuse until peer loads finish. The workers use the existing DMA
backend for transfers.

The rebased base also includes the upstream prefix-cacheable-group handling from
[#56810](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56810). This PR consumes that
group eligibility behavior and adds cross-DP publication; it does not duplicate
the upstream hybrid-model bug fix.

| Production file | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py` | Parse and validate `cpu_offload_shared`; connect worker and scheduler handshakes. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_offload.py` (new) | Discover local DP peers, verify cache identity/layout, and allocate shared KV views per TP coordinate. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_block_pool.py` (new) | Add shared hash publication, slot versions, locking and peer read references to `BlockPool`. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/metadata.py` | Define the worker-to-scheduler shared-pool handshake. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` | Attach the shared pool and synchronize scheduler lookup, allocation and completion handling. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py` | Allocate/pin shared CPU views, expose the handshake and release mappings on shutdown. |

Tests and documentation changed:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py`
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`

## Why this is not a duplicate

The following open PRs address adjacent behavior, but none adds cross-DP CPU
prefix publication and peer loading for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`:

- [#53073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53073) targets shared mmap
  startup ownership and cleanup. This PR targets completed-prefix visibility
  and safe peer reads after asynchronous DMA. It follows the mmap lifetime
  rules but adds a different metadata publication and reader-lifetime protocol.
- [#53474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53474) targets node-local
  sizing and worker placement for native `OffloadingConnector`. This PR targets
  node-local prefix reuse for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, including one pool
  per TP coordinate. The connectors, allocation path and target behavior differ;
  this PR has no code dependency on #53474.
- [#47324](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47324) targets a GPU
  load/compute stream race inside one worker. This PR targets host-side slot
  ownership when another worker reads a completed prefix. It does not implement
  the open PR's load-path stream-ordering fix; the two changes are complementary,
  and this PR adds separate cross-worker reader references.
- [#57418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418) targets concurrent
  requests waiting for the same in-flight load inside one engine. This PR
  targets completed CPU prefixes shared by different DP engines; it does not
  change connector-side coalescing of simultaneous loads.
- [#43483](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43483) targets routing a
  request to the DP rank that already owns a GPU prefix. This PR targets actual
  CPU KV publication and peer loading when routing selects another replica;
  routing-only ownership hints cannot provide that transfer.
- [#57422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57422) targets inode-safe
  unlinking of existing shared mmap files. This PR uses the existing mmap
  lifetime model but adds cross-DP prefix metadata and reader references.
- [#54743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54743) targets which KV
  groups receive offload configuration. This PR keeps the existing group
  eligibility rules and adds sharing only for groups already handled by
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`.
- [#52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921) targets aligning
  scheduler and worker pool sizes across PP/speculative workers. This PR keeps
  the existing per-worker capacity calculation and adds node-local sharing
  after those capacities agree.

## Validation

Validation was run on `b9b640c09dd7ace867f84077902567c5625cad06`, based on
upstream `3e2a7e74a556623ddee3a327299d7bf04055501e`.
The current branch commit `c7756cf854aad81a6adb5d4c749886c96fb5b3d4` rebases
that version onto upstream `dd30786fef8b15bd83205833c7b3348b0ba0ebc7`;
conflict resolutions and a type-checking adjustment are limited to tests,
leaving this PR's implementation patch unchanged.

On the rebased source, the focused scheduler, KV-event and connector suite passed
**135 tests** on the DGX Spark CUDA environment:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

The suite includes shared scheduler publication, reader pinning, delayed
publication, metadata mismatch rejection, non-prefix-cacheable groups and the
TP configuration acceptance test. Ruff and the applicable pre-commit checks pass.

The model validation used two DGX Spark hosts, each with one NVIDIA GB10
(SM121), CUDA 13.2, driver 580.173.02, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. Because only two physical GPUs were available, the
model tests used a diagnostic topology with two logical workers per GPU. This
is functional evidence, not independent-GPU performance evidence; PyTorch
requires NCCL processes to have exclusive GPU access.

All TTFT and GSM8K results below use the TP2×DP2 topology described above.

For the TP2×DP2 diagnostic, the four logical workers were mapped as follows:

| Logical launch rank | DP | TP | Host | HTTP port |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP0 endpoint |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |
| 2 | 1 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP1 endpoint |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |

The TP shard probe restored distinct TP0 and TP1 byte patterns through their
corresponding local DP groups and passed the all-shard publication barrier.
The full model run used DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DSpark K5 probabilistic
sampling, CUDA graphs, Rust frontend, RoCE and 2 GiB CPU/GPU KV capacity per
worker.

### Experiment setup

Use the same source commit and model weights for both modes. The launch below
shows the TP2×DP2 settings used for the TP shard and recovery probe. Run one
process for each logical launch rank in the table above: ranks 0 and 2 on the
first host, and ranks 1 and 3 on the second. Here `--nnodes 4` counts four logical
launches across two physical hosts; the DP size is 2.

Set `MODEL` to the
[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731)
weights, then set `NODE_RANK`, `DP_RANK`, `DP_PORT` and the coordinator ports and
address for the deployment. Use distinct HTTP ports for DP0 and DP1, one shared
DP RPC port, and one shared TP master port. Logical ranks 1 and 3 are headless.
The host-specific network environment is intentionally omitted.

```bash
KV_CONFIG='{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_offload_shared":true,"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":2147483648,"lazy_offload":false}}'

PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$DP_PORT" \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-rank "$DP_RANK" \
  --data-parallel-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-address "$HEAD_IP" --data-parallel-rpc-port "$DP_RPC_PORT" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter \
  --nnodes 4 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$HEAD_IP" --master-port "$TP_MASTER_PORT" \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.47 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV_CONFIG"
```

Add `--headless` for logical ranks 1 and 3. For the private control, change only
`cpu_offload_shared` to `false`. Keep `expandable_segments:False` in both
connector runs because the upstream KV-connector guard rejects
`expandable_segments:True`.

External DP routing gives one configured endpoint port to DP0 and another to DP1
on the coordinator host; the TP followers are headless. Send case `i` to DP rank
`i % 2` for the cold phase and to `1 - (i % 2)` for the peer phase, preserving
the prompt and `cache_salt`. The port selects the replica; it is not part of the
prefix hash.
Between phases, wait for requests and stores to finish, then POST to
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` on both endpoints for a cold run, or
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` to clear only GPU caches before peer
replay. Check that both resets succeed before issuing requests. Confirm reuse
with the external CPU-prefix counters.

### Offload correctness and latency

The GPU DMA tests and TP2 shard probe restored distinct TP0/TP1 byte patterns
after peer loads and withheld publication until all TP workers completed their
stores.

#### Performance improvement test

The rebased-source one-shot test used 24 unique approximately 6K-token prefixes,
one in-flight request per endpoint and streaming `max_tokens=1` requests. Each
prefix was populated on its owner, GPU caches were reset, and the prefix was
requested exactly once from its local DP peer.

| Mode | Peer TTFT p50 | Peer TTFT p95 | External transfer | Local compute |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private | 9.17 s | 12.22 s | 0 / 140,652 | 140,652 |
| Shared | 4.91 s | 9.29 s | 129,024 / 140,652 | 11,628 |

Shared peer TTFT was 46.4% lower in this rebased-source diagnostic run. All 24
peer requests had zero errors, empty outputs, replacement characters,
invalid controls or cold/peer output mismatches. This is a diagnostic result;
the topology with two logical workers per GB10 is not a production throughput
setup.

### Accuracy validation

The rebased-source GSM8K evaluation used three fresh cold/peer pairs with the
same 200 five-shot questions, `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, concurrency 32 and a
512-token output limit:

| Configuration | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Mean | Min–max | DSpark acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private cold | 189 | 189 | 189 | 94.50% | 94.50–94.50% | 64.10% |
| Private peer | 191 | 189 | 190 | 95.00% | 94.50–95.50% | 64.20% |
| Shared cold | 188 | 189 | 189 | 94.33% | 94.00–94.50% | 63.94% |
| Shared peer | 190 | 190 | 189 | 94.83% | 94.50–95.00% | 64.60% |

All 2,400 requests completed without request errors, empty output, replacement
characters or invalid control characters. These repeated evaluations show normal
serving-workload variation and are not a statistical equivalence claim. The
TP2×DP2 recovery probe separately passed 8/8 cold and 8/8 peer requests in both
modes with token-exact output; private peer CPU hits were 0 and shared peer CPU
hits were 45,056 tokens. The independent TP-shard/publication probe also passed.

## AI assistance

The implementation and analysis were assisted with AI and reviewed by human.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Focused on KV events only. Stores and removals stay owner-scoped and balanced: only the writer rank inserts or evicts its partition, peers import and drop index entries through the `super()` helpers without events, and `take_events` relabels `BlockRemoved` to `kv_event_medium`/`LOCAL`. So the per-copy contract holds in steady state.

The gap is reset. `SharedCPUBlockPool.reset_prefix_cache` clears `_hash_counts` for every local partition but only the resetting rank queues `AllBlocksCleared`. Peers then drop their own slots' hashes in `_refresh_hashes` via `_remove_cached_block_hashes`, which emits nothing, and later evictions of those slots find no hash, so the peer never emits a `BlockRemoved` either. Consumers (llm-d `pool.go`, Dynamo `zmq_wire`) scope `AllBlocksCleared` to the emitting publisher and DP rank, so the peer's `CPU` entries stay stale until it restarts. With the internal-LB client the reset fans out and each rank usually emits its own clear, but it leaks with external DP LB when only one endpoint is reset, and when one rank's reset succeeds while a peer's returns `false` after its refresh already dropped the hashes.

Wonder if we could either scope reset to the local partition, so each rank's `AllBlocksCleared` covers exactly what it cleared, or keep the shared reset and have a peer queue its own `AllBlocksCleared` when `_refresh_hashes` observes a foreign reset (e.g. a reset generation in the header). A shared-mode case in `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py` that resets on the writer and checks the reader's events would pin it.

This clears every local DP rank's slots but only this rank's publisher emits `AllBlocksCleared`, so peers' earlier `BlockStored` (medium `CPU`) are never withdrawn: `AllBlocksCleared` is scoped to publisher plus DP rank on the consumer side. I think either clearing only `[self._start, self._end)` here, or signalling a reset generation that peers turn into their own `AllBlocksCleared`, would keep the events consistent.

+    def _sync_peer_pins(self) -> None:
+        refs = self._refs[self._start + 1 : self._end]
+        pinned = {
+            self._start + 1 + int(i)
+            for i in np.flatnonzero(refs > 0)
+            if self.blocks[self._start + 1 + int(i)].ref_cnt == 0
+        }
+        for slot in pinned - self._peer_pinned:
+            self.free_block_queue.remove(self.blocks[slot])
+        for slot in self._peer_pinned - pinned:
+            if self.blocks[slot].ref_cnt == 0:
+                self.free_block_queue.append(self.blocks[slot])
+        self._peer_pinned = pinned
+
+    def get_num_free_blocks(self) -> int:
+        with self.locked():
+            self._sync_peer_pins()
+            return super().get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    def get_cached_block(
+        self, block_hash: BlockHash, kv_cache_group_ids: list[int]
+    ) -> list[KVCacheBlock] | None:
+        blocks = super().get_cached_block(block_hash, kv_cache_group_ids)
+        if blocks is None:
+            return None
+        # A process can exit between invalidating hashes and publishing a new
+        # revision. Check shared readiness even when the local index is current.
+        for block in blocks:
+            slot = block.block_id
+            if (
+                self._refs[slot] < 0
+                or self._hash_counts[slot] == 0
+                or self._versions[slot] != self._seen[slot]
+            ):
+                return None
+        return blocks
+

+        with self.locked():
+            blocks = super().get_new_blocks(num_blocks)
+            for block in blocks:
+                self._refs[block.block_id] = -1
+            return blocks
+

+        slot = block.block_id
+        assert self._start < slot < self._end
+        self._hash_counts[slot] = 0
+        self._changed(slot)
+        return super()._maybe_evict_cached_block(block)
+
+    def _insert_block_hash(
+        self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId, block: KVCacheBlock, num_tokens: int | None
+    ) -> None:
+        with self.locked():
+            slot = block.block_id
+            assert self._start < slot < self._end
+            if self.cached_block_hash_to_block.contain(key, slot):
+                return
+            count = int(self._hash_counts[slot])
+            if count >= self._hashes.shape[1] or len(key) != self._hashes.shape[2]:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Shared CPU offload slot hash metadata exceeds its layout."
+                )
+            super()._insert_block_hash(key, block, num_tokens)
+            self._hashes[slot, count] = np.frombuffer(key, dtype=np.uint8)
+            if count == 0:
+                self._num_tokens[slot] = num_tokens if num_tokens is not None else -1
+                self._refs[slot] = block.ref_cnt
+            self._hash_counts[slot] = count + 1
+            self._changed(slot)
+
+    def touch(self, blocks: Sequence[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
+        with self.locked():
+            for block in blocks:
+                if block.is_null:
+                    continue
+                slot = block.block_id
+                assert self._refs[slot] >= 0
+                if (
+                    self._start < slot < self._end
+                    and block.ref_cnt == 0
+                    and slot not in self._peer_pinned
+                ):
+                    self.free_block_queue.remove(block)
+                block.ref_cnt += 1
+                self._refs[slot] += 1
+
+    def free_blocks(self, ordered_blocks: Iterable[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
+        with self.locked():
+            owned = []
+            for block in ordered_blocks:
+                if block.is_null:
+                    continue
+                slot = block.block_id
+                assert block.ref_cnt > 0
+                refs = self._refs[slot]
+                self._refs[slot] = 0 if refs == -1 else refs - 1
+                if self._start < slot < self._end:
+                    owned.append(block)
+                else:
+                    block.ref_cnt -= 1
+            super().free_blocks(owned)
+            self._peer_pinned.difference_update(
+                b.block_id for b in owned if b.ref_cnt == 0
+            )
+            self._sync_peer_pins()
+
+    def reset_prefix_cache(self) -> bool:
+        with self.locked():
+            if np.any(self._refs != 0):
+                return False
+            self._hash_counts[:] = 0
+            self._header[0] += 1
+            self._versions[:] = self._header[0]
+            self._seen[:] = self._versions
+            self._seen_revision = int(self._header[0])
+            self.cached_block_hash_to_block = BlockHashToBlockMap()
+            self.cached_block_hashes_by_block.clear()
+            for block in self.blocks:
+                block.reset_hash()
+            if self.enable_kv_cache_events:
+                self.kv_event_queue.append(AllBlocksCleared())

+is reserved as a null block. Capacity cannot be borrowed from another writer's
+partition, and simultaneous stores of the same prefix can occupy multiple slots.

+shared-memory visibility at startup. Schedulers keep the existing `BlockPool`

+makes lookup and pinning atomic across processes. A slot is published only after
+its store completes and cannot be reused while another engine is loading it.

+own KV shard with the corresponding TP rank in local DP replicas. Pipeline and
+context parallelism are currently unsupported (`PP=DCP=PCP=1`) because their

detail.body:
# [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas

## Summary

Implement #58240. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` currently keeps an independent CPU prefix cache
in each DP replica. When a request is routed to another local replica, that replica recomputes
a prefix even though a completed CPU copy is available. This change adds an opt-in
`cpu_offload_shared=true` mode that lets local DP replicas reuse completed CPU prefixes.

This builds on [#37160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37160), which
introduced `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` and its private per-replica CPU cache.
This PR extends that connector with opt-in cross-DP publication and lookup; it
does not change the native offloader's per-replica semantics.

## Configuration

Add `cpu_offload_shared`, a JSON boolean in `kv_connector_extra_config`,
defaulting to `false`. Set it to `true` to share completed CPU prefixes with
compatible DP replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group.
Leaving it unset retains the existing private CPU pools.

The CPU capacity remains a per-worker budget: `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank`
reserves each worker's write partition. Corresponding local DP peers can read
published entries from one another's partitions, while writes remain owned by
the worker that allocates the slot. For example, two local DP peers configured
with 8 GiB each expose a 16 GiB node-local region for published slots and
metadata; this is shared visibility, not a dynamically rebalanced write pool.

Pass the following to `--kv-transfer-config`:

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "cpu_offload_shared": true,
    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
    "lazy_offload": false
  }
}
```

Shared mode requires the CPU backend, eager offloading (`lazy_offload=false`),
prefix caching, compatible model/KV layouts and reproducible prefix hashes.
It supports fixed MoE DP groups and TP, with `PP=DCP=PCP=1` and no LoRA or
elastic EP. Each TP coordinate shares its own KV shard with corresponding
local DP peers. Cross-node transfer requires a network-capable connector or tier.

## Implementation

Use the existing `SharedOffloadRegion` type, as established for native
`CPUOffloadingSpec` storage by
[#50094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50094), and the DMA/`BlockPool`
interfaces for storage and transfers; the cross-DP publication index, locking
and reader reference semantics are new code in this PR. Each writer owns a
fixed partition, and the shared pool does not dynamically move free write slots
between workers. Lookup and pinning use `flock` on the metadata region's descriptor;
prefixes are published after all worker stores complete, and reader references
prevent slot reuse until peer loads finish. The workers use the existing DMA
backend for transfers.

The rebased base also includes the upstream prefix-cacheable-group handling from
[#56810](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56810). This PR consumes that
group eligibility behavior and adds cross-DP publication; it does not duplicate
the upstream hybrid-model bug fix.

| Production file | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py` | Parse and validate `cpu_offload_shared`; connect worker and scheduler handshakes. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_offload.py` (new) | Discover local DP peers, verify cache identity/layout, and allocate shared KV views per TP coordinate. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_block_pool.py` (new) | Add shared hash publication, slot versions, locking and peer read references to `BlockPool`. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/metadata.py` | Define the worker-to-scheduler shared-pool handshake. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` | Attach the shared pool and synchronize scheduler lookup, allocation and completion handling. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py` | Allocate/pin shared CPU views, expose the handshake and release mappings on shutdown. |

Tests and documentation changed:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py`
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`

## Why this is not a duplicate

The following open PRs address adjacent behavior, but none adds cross-DP CPU
prefix publication and peer loading for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`:

- [#53073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53073) targets shared mmap
  startup ownership and cleanup. This PR targets completed-prefix visibility
  and safe peer reads after asynchronous DMA. It follows the mmap lifetime
  rules but adds a different metadata publication and reader-lifetime protocol.
- [#53474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53474) targets node-local
  sizing and worker placement for native `OffloadingConnector`. This PR targets
  node-local prefix reuse for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, including one pool
  per TP coordinate. The connectors, allocation path and target behavior differ;
  this PR has no code dependency on #53474.
- [#47324](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47324) targets a GPU
  load/compute stream race inside one worker. This PR targets host-side slot
  ownership when another worker reads a completed prefix. It does not implement
  the open PR's load-path stream-ordering fix; the two changes are complementary,
  and this PR adds separate cross-worker reader references.
- [#57418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418) targets concurrent
  requests waiting for the same in-flight load inside one engine. This PR
  targets completed CPU prefixes shared by different DP engines; it does not
  change connector-side coalescing of simultaneous loads.
- [#43483](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43483) targets routing a
  request to the DP rank that already owns a GPU prefix. This PR targets actual
  CPU KV publication and peer loading when routing selects another replica;
  routing-only ownership hints cannot provide that transfer.
- [#57422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57422) targets inode-safe
  unlinking of existing shared mmap files. This PR uses the existing mmap
  lifetime model but adds cross-DP prefix metadata and reader references.
- [#54743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54743) targets which KV
  groups receive offload configuration. This PR keeps the existing group
  eligibility rules and adds sharing only for groups already handled by
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`.

  scheduler and worker pool sizes across PP/speculative workers. This PR keeps
  the existing per-worker capacity calculation and adds node-local sharing
  after those capacities agree.

Validation was run on `b9b640c09dd7ace867f84077902567c5625cad06`, based on
upstream `3e2a7e74a556623ddee3a327299d7bf04055501e`.
The current branch commit `c7756cf854aad81a6adb5d4c749886c96fb5b3d4` rebases
that version onto upstream `dd30786fef8b15bd83205833c7b3348b0ba0ebc7`;
conflict resolutions and a type-checking adjustment are limited to tests,
leaving this PR's implementation patch unchanged.

On the rebased source, the focused scheduler, KV-event and connector suite passed
**135 tests** on the DGX Spark CUDA environment:

```bash

  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \

  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \

publication, metadata mismatch rejection, non-prefix-cacheable groups and the
TP configuration acceptance test. Ruff and the applicable pre-commit checks pass.

(SM121), CUDA 13.2, driver 580.173.02, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. Because only two physical GPUs were available, the
model tests used a diagnostic topology with two logical workers per GPU. This
is functional evidence, not independent-GPU performance evidence; PyTorch
requires NCCL processes to have exclusive GPU access.

corresponding local DP groups and passed the all-shard publication barrier.
The full model run used DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DSpark K5 probabilistic

The GPU DMA tests and TP2 shard probe restored distinct TP0/TP1 byte patterns
after peer loads and withheld publication until all TP workers completed their
stores.

The rebased-source one-shot test used 24 unique approximately 6K-token prefixes,
one in-flight request per endpoint and streaming `max_tokens=1` requests. Each
prefix was populated on its owner, GPU caches were reset, and the prefix was
requested exactly once from its local DP peer.

+## Sharing SimpleCPUOffloadConnector across local DP ranks
+
+`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` can optionally share CPU KV contents between MoE data
+parallel replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group. A request
+routed to another local DP replica can reuse a completed CPU prefix without the
+router knowing which replica originally computed it.
+
+For example, for eight local GPUs with TP1 and expert parallelism:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> \
+  --data-parallel-size 8 \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+  --enable-expert-parallel \
+  --enable-prefix-caching \
+  --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256 \
+  --kv-transfer-config '{
+    "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
+    "kv_role": "kv_both",
+    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+      "cpu_offload_shared": true,
+      "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
+      "lazy_offload": false
+    }
+  }'
+```
+
+`cpu_offload_shared` defaults to `false`. Shared mode currently uses eager
+offloading only. Each local rank retains its configured write capacity
+and owns a fixed partition of slots; it can read completed blocks from every
+local partition. The example allocates approximately 64 GiB of CPU KV memory
+per node, plus index metadata. Size `/dev/shm` accordingly. One slot per partition
+is reserved as a null block. Capacity cannot be borrowed from another writer's
+partition, and simultaneous stores of the same prefix can occupy multiple slots.
+
+The workers use `SharedOffloadRegion` for the pinned KV allocation and verify
+shared-memory visibility at startup. Schedulers keep the existing `BlockPool`
+hash indexes and LRU queues. A second shared region stores slot hashes,
+publication revisions and offloading's `ChunkStatus` references. File locking
+makes lookup and pinning atomic across processes. A slot is published only after
+its store completes and cannot be reused while another engine is loading it.
+No collective operations run on the per-request offload path.
+
+The shared implementation supports tensor parallelism: each TP rank shares its
+own KV shard with the corresponding TP rank in local DP replicas. Pipeline and
+context parallelism are currently unsupported (`PP=DCP=PCP=1`) because their
+KV ownership and block-coordinate semantics require a separate design. There
+are no LoRA adapter support guarantees. The backend must be `cpu`. All replicas
+must agree on the model, KV layout, capacity, prefix hash algorithm, and hash
+seed. SHA-256 variants work with the default seed; xxHash variants require the
+same numeric `PYTHONHASHSEED` on every replica. Incompatible configurations fail
+at startup. Cache salts continue to isolate request prefixes.
+
+Sharing is **node-local**. A two-node DP2/TP1/EP deployment with one GPU per node
+creates two independent pools and cannot reuse one node's CPU KV on the other.
+That topology validates distributed serving and isolation; testing local DP
+reuse additionally requires multiple engine processes in one IPC namespace.
+Cross-node KV movement requires a network-capable connector or tier.
+Independent non-MoE replicas and separately launched deployments with their own
+distributed groups do not join this pool.
+
+A successful prefix-cache reset clears all local partitions. Reset returns
+`false` while shared transfer references remain. Each launch creates a fresh
+namespace; cached data is not reused after restart. The KV and index files are
+unlinked after their workers or schedulers attach. Their open file descriptors
+retain the mappings and metadata lock until process termination. A crash before
+attachment finishes can leave a named mmap for cleanup after the deployment
+stops. A live peer retains a crashed engine's transfer references because its
+worker may still be using the slots.
+

+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if self._closed:

+        blocks_per_rank,
+        region.total_size_bytes / 1024**3,
+    )
+    return region, cpu_caches, metadata

+                )
+            self._seen[slot] = self._versions[slot]
+        self._seen_revision = revision
+
+    def _changed(self, slot: int) -> None:
+        self._header[0] += 1
+        self._versions[slot] = self._header[0]
+        self._seen[slot] = self._versions[slot]
+
+    def _sync_peer_pins(self) -> None:
+        refs = self._refs[self._start + 1 : self._end]
+        pinned = {
+            self._start + 1 + int(i)
+            for i in np.flatnonzero(refs > 0)
+            if self.blocks[self._start + 1 + int(i)].ref_cnt == 0
+        }
+        for slot in pinned - self._peer_pinned:
+            self.free_block_queue.remove(self.blocks[slot])
+        for slot in self._peer_pinned - pinned:
+            if self.blocks[slot].ref_cnt == 0:
+                self.free_block_queue.append(self.blocks[slot])
+        self._peer_pinned = pinned
+
+    def get_num_free_blocks(self) -> int:
+        with self.locked():
+            self._sync_peer_pins()
+            return super().get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    def get_cached_block(
+        self, block_hash: BlockHash, kv_cache_group_ids: list[int]
+    ) -> list[KVCacheBlock] | None:
+        blocks = super().get_cached_block(block_hash, kv_cache_group_ids)
+        if blocks is None:
+            return None
+        # A process can exit between invalidating hashes and publishing a new
+        # revision. Check shared readiness even when the local index is current.
+        for block in blocks:
+            slot = block.block_id
+            if (
+                self._refs[slot] < 0
+                or self._hash_counts[slot] == 0
+                or self._versions[slot] != self._seen[slot]
+            ):
+                return None
+        return blocks
+
+    def get_new_blocks(self, num_blocks: int) -> list[KVCacheBlock]:
+        with self.locked():
+            blocks = super().get_new_blocks(num_blocks)
+            for block in blocks:
+                self._refs[block.block_id] = -1
+            return blocks
+
+    def _maybe_evict_cached_block(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> bool:
+        slot = block.block_id
+        assert self._start < slot < self._end
+        self._hash_counts[slot] = 0
+        self._changed(slot)
+        return super()._maybe_evict_cached_block(block)
+
+    def _insert_block_hash(
+        self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId, block: KVCacheBlock, num_tokens: int | None
+    ) -> None:
+        with self.locked():
+            slot = block.block_id
+            assert self._start < slot < self._end
+            if self.cached_block_hash_to_block.contain(key, slot):
+                return
+            count = int(self._hash_counts[slot])
+            if count >= self._hashes.shape[1] or len(key) != self._hashes.shape[2]:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Shared CPU offload slot hash metadata exceeds its layout."
+                )
+            super()._insert_block_hash(key, block, num_tokens)
+            self._hashes[slot, count] = np.frombuffer(key, dtype=np.uint8)
+            if count == 0:
+                self._num_tokens[slot] = num_tokens if num_tokens is not None else -1
+                self._refs[slot] = block.ref_cnt
+            self._hash_counts[slot] = count + 1
+            self._changed(slot)
+
+    def touch(self, blocks: Sequence[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
+        with self.locked():
+            for block in blocks:
+                if block.is_null:
+                    continue
+                slot = block.block_id
+                assert self._refs[slot] >= 0
+                if (
+                    self._start < slot < self._end
+                    and block.ref_cnt == 0
+                    and slot not in self._peer_pinned
+                ):
+                    self.free_block_queue.remove(block)
+                block.ref_cnt += 1
+                self._refs[slot] += 1
+
+    def free_blocks(self, ordered_blocks: Iterable[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
+        with self.locked():
+            owned = []
+            for block in ordered_blocks:
+                if block.is_null:
+                    continue
+                slot = block.block_id
+                assert block.ref_cnt > 0
+                refs = self._refs[slot]
+                self._refs[slot] = 0 if refs == -1 else refs - 1
+                if self._start < slot < self._end:
+                    owned.append(block)
+                else:
+                    block.ref_cnt -= 1
+            super().free_blocks(owned)
+            self._peer_pinned.difference_update(
+                b.block_id for b in owned if b.ref_cnt == 0
+            )
+            self._sync_peer_pins()
+
+    def reset_prefix_cache(self) -> bool:
+        with self.locked():
+            if np.any(self._refs != 0):
+                return False
+            self._hash_counts[:] = 0
+            self._header[0] += 1
+            self._versions[:] = self._header[0]
+            self._seen[:] = self._versions
+            self._seen_revision = int(self._header[0])
+            self.cached_block_hash_to_block = BlockHashToBlockMap()
+            self.cached_block_hashes_by_block.clear()
+            for block in self.blocks:
+                block.reset_hash()
+            if self.enable_kv_cache_events:
+                self.kv_event_queue.append(AllBlocksCleared())

+## Sharing SimpleCPUOffloadConnector across local DP ranks
+
+`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` can optionally share CPU KV contents between MoE data
+parallel replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group. A request
+routed to another local DP replica can reuse a completed CPU prefix without the
+router knowing which replica originally computed it.
+
+For example, for eight local GPUs with TP1 and expert parallelism:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> \
+  --data-parallel-size 8 \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+  --enable-expert-parallel \
+  --enable-prefix-caching \
+  --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256 \
+  --kv-transfer-config '{
+    "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
+    "kv_role": "kv_both",
+    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+      "cpu_offload_shared": true,
+      "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
+      "lazy_offload": false
+    }
+  }'
+```
+
+`cpu_offload_shared` defaults to `false`. Shared mode currently uses eager
+offloading only. Each local rank retains its configured write capacity
+and owns a fixed partition of slots; it can read completed blocks from every
+local partition. The example allocates approximately 64 GiB of CPU KV memory
+per node, plus index metadata. Size `/dev/shm` accordingly. One slot per partition
+is reserved as a null block. Capacity cannot be borrowed from another writer's
+partition, and simultaneous stores of the same prefix can occupy multiple slots.
+
+The workers use `SharedOffloadRegion` for the pinned KV allocation and verify
+shared-memory visibility at startup. Schedulers keep the existing `BlockPool`
+hash indexes and LRU queues. A second shared region stores slot hashes,
+publication revisions and offloading's `ChunkStatus` references. File locking
+makes lookup and pinning atomic across processes. A slot is published only after
+its store completes and cannot be reused while another engine is loading it.
+No collective operations run on the per-request offload path.
+
+The shared implementation supports tensor parallelism: each TP rank shares its
+own KV shard with the corresponding TP rank in local DP replicas. Pipeline and
+context parallelism are currently unsupported (`PP=DCP=PCP=1`) because their
+KV ownership and block-coordinate semantics require a separate design. There
+are no LoRA adapter support guarantees. The backend must be `cpu`. All replicas
+must agree on the model, KV layout, capacity, prefix hash algorithm, and hash
+seed. SHA-256 variants work with the default seed; xxHash variants require the
+same numeric `PYTHONHASHSEED` on every replica. Incompatible configurations fail
+at startup. Cache salts continue to isolate request prefixes.
+
+Sharing is **node-local**. A two-node DP2/TP1/EP deployment with one GPU per node
+creates two independent pools and cannot reuse one node's CPU KV on the other.
+That topology validates distributed serving and isolation; testing local DP
+reuse additionally requires multiple engine processes in one IPC namespace.
+Cross-node KV movement requires a network-capable connector or tier.
+Independent non-MoE replicas and separately launched deployments with their own
+distributed groups do not join this pool.
+
+A successful prefix-cache reset clears all local partitions. Reset returns

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Focused on KV events only. Stores and removals stay owner-scoped and balanced: only the writer rank inserts or evicts its partition, peers import and drop index entries through the `super()` helpers without events, and `take_events` relabels `BlockRemoved` to `kv_event_medium`/`LOCAL`. So the per-copy contract holds in steady state.

The gap is reset. `SharedCPUBlockPool.reset_prefix_cache` clears `_hash_counts` for every local partition but only the resetting rank queues `AllBlocksCleared`. Peers then drop their own slots' hashes in `_refresh_hashes` via `_remove_cached_block_hashes`, which emits nothing, and later evictions of those slots find no hash, so the peer never emits a `BlockRemoved` either. Consumers (llm-d `pool.go`, Dynamo `zmq_wire`) scope `AllBlocksCleared` to the emitting publisher and DP rank, so the peer's `CPU` entries stay stale until it restarts. With the internal-LB client the reset fans out and each rank usually emits its own clear, but it leaks with external DP LB when only one endpoint is reset, and when one rank's reset succeeds while a peer's returns `false` after its refresh already dropped the hashes.

Wonder if we could either scope reset to the local partition, so each rank's `AllBlocksCleared` covers exactly what it cleared, or keep the shared reset and have a peer queue its own `AllBlocksCleared` when `_refresh_hashes` observes a foreign reset (e.g. a reset generation in the header). A shared-mode case in `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py` that resets on the writer and checks the reader's events would pin it.
